author: TEDx Talks
description:
We've optimized everything: our calendars, our workouts, even our sleep. But somehow, friendship, the thing that actually makes life feel good, has become optional.

In this talk, Matt Ritter (aka “The Friendship Guy”) makes the case that friendship isn't a personality trait, it's a habit, and one of the most underrated advantages in modern life. Drawing on insights from the 85-year Harvard Study of Adult Development, he reframes friendship as a core pillar of health, not a nice to have.

After becoming a dad and feeling his own friendships start to drift, Matt did something unexpected: he went out and made a new best friend at 45. Not through some grand gesture...but through small, repeatable moments that actually fit into real life.

Drawing from that experience, he breaks down why most adults struggle to maintain connection and introduces a simple, practical system for fixing it, including:

• Why friendship works like a muscle and how to build it through small daily reps
• How to
title: A lonely dad's guide to making new friends | Matt Ritter | TEDxEustis

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if - at the end of your life - you discovered you had spent decades looking at your phone? In this personal and thought-provoking talk, a teenager who has chosen not to own a smartphone explores how social media algorithms are designed to capture our attention and shape our habits. While recognising the benefits of technology, Seren argues that constant digital consumption can come at the expense of creativity, hobbies and real-world relationships. She urges us to live intentionally, making conscious choices about how we spend our time. ‘Lifetime Stats and Your Phone’.
Seren, an academic and drama scholar, has a particular passion for drama, maths, and science and enjoys debating, engineering and creative problem-solving. Outside the classroom, she is an enthusiastic swimmer and lacrosse player who loves reading - especially crime fiction and classic literature. Her other interests include watercolour painting, baking and piano. Through her talk, Seren hopes to encourage others t
title: Lifetime Stats and Your Phone | Seren Upton | TEDxSt Swithuns School

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if everything we have ever seen or encountered makes up just five per cent of reality?
In this fascinating exploration of dark energy, the speaker takes us on a journey through one of the greatest discoveries in modern physics: the realisation that the expansion of the universe is accelerating. Explaining complex scientific ideas through accessible examples, Alexis unpacks the differences between dark matter and dark energy, examines how these discoveries challenge our understanding of gravity, and explores the theories scientists are developing to explain the invisible forces shaping the cosmos. Alexis also looks ahead to future missions, including the next generation of space telescopes designed to uncover the secrets of the hidden universe. More than a lesson in astrophysics, her talk is a reminder that humanity's greatest breakthroughs often begin with questions about what we cannot yet see.  ‘The Mysteries of Dark Energy’. 
Alexis first discovered her interest in theoretical
title: The mysteries of dark energy | Alexis Baker | TEDxSt Swithuns School

author: TEDx Talks
description: What does a high rate of female literacy mean if working women remain unsafe and financially insecure? Drawing on her interviews in Hunza and Ghizer, Dr. Sara Rizvi Jafree examines the daily realities of women tourist guides and entrepreneurs in Gilgit-Baltistan. They describe seasonal earnings, dangerous travel, inadequate insurance, unpaid care work and community pressure. They also propose their own solutions: locally owned workspaces near home, childcare, stronger social protection, reliable healthcare and a greater say in economic decisions. Jafree asks researchers and policymakers to listen to these proposals instead of treating women’s endurance as a substitute for support. Her central argument is that useful development policy must respond to the people it serves, allowing women to earn a living without giving up their families, identities and values.  Researcher, Educator, Advocate This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized
title: Working Women's Culture & Regional Protective Policies | Dr. Sara Rizvi Jafree | TEDxFCCU Women

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Most people start over because they have to. Kenny Lee did it on purpose, at 40, with no crisis forcing a change.
His path had already run from a corporate career to founding a startup, then back to school at MIT. There he wrote down three rules for whatever came next: Choose impact. Choose hard. Choose unknown. The rules took him into agriculture—an industry he knew nothing about—and to building autonomous, solar-powered robots that pull weeds, his bet on a more sustainable way to farm.
Years in, he realized the rules weren’t his. He’d learned them as a kid, watching his father, who left Korea at 38 with a career and a country behind him, and kept choosing to begin again for the rest of his life.
This talk is about what it costs to become a beginner on purpose, and why the absence of guarantees might be the point. It asks how you measure a life when the scoreboard isn’t what you accomplished, but who and what is different because you were here. Kenny Lee is the co-founder and CEO of
title: Why I started over when I didn't have to | Kenny Lee | TEDxFargo

author: TEDx Talks
description: Wherever someone is protecting the planet, there is a story people are hungry to hear. And yet, our newsfeeds are filled with influencers peddling consumer products and rage bait. A successful media entrepreneur turned his attention to leveraging the attention economy to share the stories of gamechangers in the conservation world. Through a series of campaigns, the channel funnels support and funds to drive meaningful change around the world.  Markus Gilles is a serial entrepreneur with a background in both the NGO and tech sectors, and a sociologist by training. After exiting a German media startup and spending time in New York, Markus took a break from startup life and backpacked from Alaska to Patagonia. What started as a desire to explore our natural planet turned into a mission to save it. Seeing firsthand how our ecosystems have come under threat, Markus co-founded Planet Wild to help protect and restore wildlife and wild places through an innovative crowdfunding media model. Th
title: How we turned YouTube attention into wildlife protection | Markus Gilles | TEDxBoston

author: TEDx Talks
description: In her talk, Hannah Hembree Bell challenges us to stop settling for a life that’s comfortable enough but not deeply fulfilling. She explores the connection between what we want, what we believe we’re worth, and what we’re willing to do differently, offering a framework for moving from settling to intentional living. Hannah Hembree Bell is the founder and CEO of Hembree Bell Law, an Austin-based family law firm she built from her kitchen table after navigating her own difficult divorce and custody battle. What began as a solo practice has grown into one of the fastest-growing family law firms in the country, ranked #876 on the Inc. 5000, placing it among the top 20 fastest-growing law firms nationwide and #2 in Texas, and recognized on the 2026 Inc. Regionals for the Southwest. Through her leadership and lived experience, Hannah is passionate about helping others move through difficult transitions with courage, clarity, and intention. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED c
title: How to leave the medium-suck life behind | Hannah Hembree Bell | TEDxRound Rock Women

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What is the psychology behind risk-taking and why is stepping outside our comfort zone key to personal growth? Drawing on psychological research and real-world examples, this young speaker examines how personality, peer influence and brain development shape our willingness to take risks, particularly during adolescence.
Belle highlights how meaningful risks can build confidence, resilience, and self-discovery, distinguishing between reckless impulsivity and calculated decision-making. Through personal reflection and scientific insight, she encourages us to embrace uncertainty, learn from failure, and recognise that growth often begins at the edge of discomfort.  ‘The Joy of Risk’.
Belle loves to push herself beyond her comfort zone, whether through learning an extra language or researching science beyond the classroom.  A regular participant in academic enrichment activities, she is also a keen lacrosse player and a key member of the school choir and rock band, regularly performing in
title: The joy of risk | Belle Lam | TEDxSt Swithuns School

author: TEDx Talks
description:
When does online gaming blur the line between entertainment and gambling? Using a popular gacha game as a case study, this young speaker examines how random rewards, limited-time content, and in-game purchases are designed to keep players engaged and spending. Sophie combines personal experience with research on gaming addiction and gambling psychology to highlight the risks these systems can pose, particularly for young people. While acknowledging that gaming can be a positive and enjoyable hobby, Sophie encourages us to recognise manipulative design tactics and think carefully about how we play. ‘When Gaming Becomes Gambling’.
Sophie is best known at St Swithun’s for her passion for music. Diploma-level in piano, she regularly performs at concerts, competitions, festivals and recitals. Her favourite subjects are English, chemistry, and physics but she is also fascinated by politics, economics, and psychology. These broad interests are reflected in her holding academic, music, maths,
title: When gaming becomes gambling | Sophie Meng | TEDxSt Swithuns School

author: TEDx Talks
description:
A young film enthusiast explores how the cinematic experience has evolved for a generation shaped by streaming, social media and algorithms. She reflects on the importance of diverse storytelling, the changing role of technology, and the risk of valuing spectacle over substance. Drawing on examples from classic and modern cinema, Alice highlights how films can challenge stereotypes, shape culture, and forge human connections. She argues that as cinema continues to develop, we must not lose sight of what makes it unique: its power to capture our full attention and bring us together through shared stories. ‘Why Cinema Matters’.
Driven by her interest in culture, Alice is passionate about theatre and film. She is studying drama, religious studies, and English at A-level alongside writing a research project on method acting. Her acting experience includes taking part in a BBC production and playing lead roles in musical theatre productions. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TE
title: Why Cinema Matters | Alice Odili | TEDxSt Swithuns School

author: TEDx Talks
description:

نحن لا نبني المدن... المدن هي التي تبنينا. 
​فالعمران لا يصمم الشوارع فحسب، بل يصمم السلوك البشري و"احتمالات اللقاء" عبر تفاصيل بسيطة كمْسار دراجات أو مقعد في ساحة عامة، خالقاً ما يمكن تسميته بـ "تأثير الفراشة العمراني" الذي قد يغير حياة إنسان بالكامل.
 كاديمية وخبيرة تنفيذيّة في مجال التخطيط العمراني والإقليمي، تشغل حالياً منصب عضو المكتب التنفيذي في محافظة حماة ومدير إدارة دعم القرار والتخطيط الإقليمي بالمحافظة، إلى جانب عضويتها في المجلس الاستشاري لمحافظة حماة. تجمع في مسيرتها بين العمل التنفيذي الميداني والبحث العلمي الأكاديمي، حيث تعمل كـباحثة دكتوراه متخصصة في التخطيط العمراني ومحاضرة في كلية الهندسة المعمارية، بالإضافة إلى نشاطها المهني النقابي كـعضو في لجنة العمارة بنقابة المهندسين . تسعى من خلال أدوارها المتعددة إلى تطوير الرؤى الإستراتيجية للتنمية التنموية والعمرانية، ودعم صناعة القرار الم
title: العمران و الإنسان :لماذا تشعر بالغربة في مدينة تعرفها جيدا | راوية محمد | TEDxAl Wady

author: TEDx Talks
description: Is being nice always the right thing to do? Laura Papworth challenges the common belief that kindness and niceness are the same, arguing that true kindness often requires honesty, courage, and a willingness to embrace discomfort. Through relatable everyday situations, she explores why choosing what helps someone most isn't always the easiest option, but it is often the most meaningful. Laura is passionate about helping people navigate an increasingly connected world with confidence and curiosity. She enjoys exploring the ways technology shapes our lives, relationships, and opportunities, and is driven by a desire to make a meaningful difference in the lives of others. Through her work and personal experiences, Laura is continually inspired by the power of learning, growth, and human connection. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Kindness Is the Braver Choice | Laura Papworth | TEDxSt Marys College Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: We spend so much of our lives striving towards an idea of what is considered “ordinary,” often believing that fitting in means being accepted, successful, or better. But who decided what ordinary is in the first place? Perhaps ordinary isn’t about fitting into a mould at all. Maybe it is simply being human — imperfect, authentic, and unapologetically yourself. I’m curious, love playing sports, and enjoy getting creative with arts and crafts. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Who Decided What Ordinary Is? | Alyssa De Souza | TEDxThe Ardee School NFC

author: TEDx Talks
description: The Mountain Doesn’t Care Who You Are explores how the labels we give ourselves often disappear when we face a challenge. The mountain doesn’t care about your achievements, your background, or how others define you. It simply asks you to take the next step. Sometimes, the journey teaches us that who we are matters less than who we choose to become along the way. I’m in year 11 living in Goa, always curious about different perspectives, people and ways of seeing life-with a love for mountains, and adrenaline driven adventure This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: The Mountain Doesn’t Care Who You Are | Kiyaah Raghuwanhsi | TEDxThe Ardee School NFC

author: TEDx Talks
description:
We talk constantly about anxiety, loneliness, and mental health, but what if these are symptoms rather than the root cause? Dr Leon Stensholm explores the growing crisis of human disconnection and argues that genuine belonging begins when people feel seen, valued, and safe to be themselves. Through the concept of creating safe spaces, he challenges us to consider whether rebuilding human connection may be one of the most powerful ways to improve wellbeing in our schools, workplaces, and communities. Dr Leon Stensholm is a nationally recognised mental health advocate, counsellor, sports nutritionist and four-time author. He was awarded an Honorary Doctorate in Arts in recognition of his contributions to suicide prevention and youth mental health and has been recognised through a number of national and regional awards for his community work.
Driven by personal experience following the loss of his brother and several clients to suicide, Leon founded Lookout07, a Sunshine Coast youth cent
title: The importance of safe spaces | Leon Stensholm | TEDxSt Marys College Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
À travers son parcours marqué par l’accident, la perte et la reconstruction, Racky Diack nous invite à porter un autre regard sur nos cicatrices, qu’elles soient visibles ou invisibles.
Son talk explore la manière dont les épreuves peuvent bouleverser notre identité, mais aussi nous obliger à nous redéfinir. La résilience n’est alors pas seulement la capacité de revenir à celle que nous étions avant : elle peut devenir l’art de se réinventer autrement.
Avec vulnérabilité et authenticité, Racky montre que le détachement, l’acceptation et la transformation peuvent devenir de véritables forces. Nos cicatrices ne racontent pas uniquement ce que nous avons perdu : elles racontent aussi qui nous sommes devenues. À la suite d’un accident qui a profondément transformé son corps et son parcours, **Racky Diack** a compris que la résilience ne consiste pas à redevenir celle que l’on était, mais à apprendre à se réinventer.

Conférencière et autrice, elle transforme aujourd’hui son expérience per
title: Nos cicatrices racontent une histoire | Racky Diack | TEDxLongueuil Women

author: TEDx Talks
description:
À travers l’histoire universelle de Sophie, Florence explore un angle mort bien réel des parcours professionnels féminins : le silence. Pourquoi tant de femmes compétentes attendent-elles de se sentir « prêtes » avant d’oser demander une promotion, une augmentation, une opportunité ou simplement leur juste place?
Dans ce talk, Florence met en lumière le coût invisible de l’attente, du doute et de l’auto-censure. Elle nous invite à repenser notre rapport à l’ambition, à la légitimité et à la prise de parole, avec une idée simple mais puissante : on n’obtient pas toujours ce que l’on mérite, mais souvent ce que l’on ose demander.
Le talk s’inscrivait très bien dans le thème « Exponentielles : De l’intime à l’universel », en partant d’une expérience individuelle pour toucher à une réalité vécue par de nombreuses femmes. Entrepreneure, conférencière et coach en transformation professionnelle, Florence est reconnue pour sa capacité à mettre des mots clairs sur des enjeux souvent tus. Elle
title: De l’expérience intime à l’impact collectif  | Florence Morin-Laurin | TEDxLongueuil Women

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Et si ce que nous vivons intimement n’était pas une faiblesse, mais une clé de transformation sociale ?
Dans ce talk, Coumba Ngom explore comment des trajectoires personnelles marquées par le décalage, l’invisibilité ou le fait de naviguer entre plusieurs mondes peuvent devenir de puissants leviers d’impact collectif. Elle montre comment l’intime peut révéler les angles morts de nos systèmes, et comment la transformation devient possible lorsque ces expériences individuelles sont reliées, structurées et inscrites dans une dynamique collective. Coumba Ngom évolue à la croisée de l’engagement citoyen, de la gouvernance et de l’entrepreneuriat social. Reconnue pour sa capacité à relier les mondes — institutionnel, communautaire et entrepreneurial — elle œuvre à transformer des enjeux complexes en leviers d’impact collectif. Son parcours, marqué par la traversée de plusieurs univers et réalités, nourrit une réflexion profonde sur la place de l’intime dans les dynamiques de changement soci
title: De l’expérience intime à l’impact collectif  | Coumba Ngom | TEDxLongueuil Women

author: TEDx Talks
description: Celine Augustine Shaw talks about cultivating viriditas—the medieval concept of the mind's sovereign greening power—as a source of planetary resilience and human growth. Drawing on quantum sensing and neuromorphic computing alongside classical art and poetry, she argues that the quality of one's love for knowledge quietly governs the quality of one's learning and one's making.  Celine Augustine Shaw is a materials engineer and intellectual architect whose work unites rigorous quantum optics with the timeless grace of classical artistry, designing across scales from the atomic to the planetary. She is also the founder of l'Ballet du Célestin, a Bay Area chamber ballet company, and finds that her technical and artistic practices spring from one quiet sanctuary. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Portrait of an Engineer as A Young Artist | Celine Shaw | TEDxUCLA

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Change can feel like the end of the story we knew, but sometimes, it is the beginning of a better one. "I am a high school student, aspiring physician scientist, and the founder of NeuroBridge, an initiative within LearnServeSmile dedicated to making neuroscience and neurological diseases more accessible to young people. My passion for neuroscience began after my father's neurological diagnosis, an experience that transformed my curiosity into a commitment to educating others and supporting families navigating similar challenges.

Beyond NeuroBridge, I am an active member of the National Speech & Debate Association (NSDA), where I compete in Original Oratory and use public speaking to inspire meaningful conversations. I am also a two-time Ohio State Science Fair qualifier, conducting independent research and exploring the intersection of science, medicine, and innovation. Through volunteering at Cincinnati Children's Hospital, TriHealth, and Kettering Health, I have gained valuable in
title: When change rewrites your story | Saanvi Ramachandran | TEDxKings Mills Youth
